analysis:
Both changed files are documentation only (docs/architecture/inference.md, docs/developer/test.md), so no executable code changed and no control was weakened. The head excerpt at inference.md lines 2022-2222 is unchanged context. The real change is the patch at lines 1030-1046. It documents a new PromptTokenCache in the provider tokenizer path, with ChatTemplateLoopRewrites for Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS, parallel encoding on up to four cores, and a DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0 kill switch. test.md adds a test recipe and a `darkbloom benchmark --prompt-prep` command.

The documentation states that token-ID reuse is scoped per prefix-cache scope and never crosses scopes. If the implementation matches, it does not widen the cross-tenant exposure in T-041, and the coordinator-authored cacheSalt isolation (A-001) would be preserved. The implementation is not in this PR's supplied evidence, so I cannot verify it. A reviewer of the code change should check the following.
- The token-ID cache is keyed by the authenticated cache scope.
- Hit-versus-miss tokenization latency does not add a new timing oracle beyond the accepted SEC-035 channel.
- Cached prompt text or tokens are held in memory only, not persisted to disk, which would bypass the HMAC and encryption posture.
- The rewritten template renders are equivalent, so prompt-contract and routing identity are unchanged.

The test.md recipe also reads PROMPT_TOKEN_CACHE_MODEL_DIRS, which is a local-only test variable. No secrets or endpoints are introduced. needs_deeper_review is true because the described feature has security-relevant isolation and timing properties that only the code can confirm.
